thread:
jordan_acme: Hey team — heads up from a customer. They report intermittent partial SSE payloads and frequent reconnects only on Safari (16/16.4 tested), behind our CDN. Token is sent via cookie. Repro below, fingers crossed for a quick fix.
suzanne_support: thanks Jordan. can you paste the exact repro steps and any response headers/logs? curious if it's CORS or the CDN returning 304s.
jordan_acme: Repro steps I gave them:
1) open Safari 16.4 on mac
2) visit app using CDN domain: https://sse.example-cdn.net/stream?room=123
3) client uses native EventSource (no custom headers) and relies on cookie auth
4) after ~10-30s they see the stream stop mid-message, EventSource fires `error` and then reconnects; when reconnecting sometimes gets only a partial JSON object and app-side parser fails
Headers they captured on the stream response (from a test on their origin):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
cache-control: max-age=0, must-revalidate
access-control-allow-origin: https://app.acme.com
access-control-allow-credentials: true
set-cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None
transfer-encoding: chunked
```
And from the CDN edge they sometimes see a 304:
```
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
cache-control: public, max-age=600
etag: "xyz"
```
max_infra: two quick things:
- EventSource doesn't support custom Authorization headers. if you rely on headers you must instead use a query param or cookie.
- Browsers require Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true + Access-Control-Allow-Origin to be exact origin (not `*`) when sending cookies. that part looks ok but Safari has stricter heuristics around SameSite & ITP.
alex_runtime: flagging a runtime/CDN interaction: if the CDN returns a 304 for an SSE endpoint, the client can treat that as an immediate end-of-response because 304 responses have no body. Some CDNs will return 304 for conditional GETs which is fine for static assets but breaks streaming endpoints. recommend ensuring the CDN bypasses caching for SSE endpoints.
alex_runtime: also note gzip/chunking interplay. If edge performs early compression normalization and then decides to revalidate, you can end up with inconsistent chunk boundaries that the EventSource parser on Safari treats as truncated messages.
suzanne_support: useful. Jordan — can you ask customer to try two quick experiments to isolate CDN vs Safari:
1) bypass CDN and hit origin directly (CNAME or host header) — does the problem go away?
2) use a simple fetch-based streaming fallback in Safari to see if readableStream shows the same truncation.
jordan_acme: they tried bypassing CDN and the issue drops from ~1/5 requests to 0/20 in their tests. so looks CDN-related. they also tried "eventsource-polyfill" and it reduced parser errors but still saw reconnects. polyfill uses XHR which has slightly different semantics.
max_infra: ok that nails it — CDN conditional caching is the culprit. mitigation options:
- Configure CDN to bypass caching for `/stream` endpoints (Cache-Control: no-store / origin-pass-through / edge-cache: none)
- Ensure origin sends `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` and optionally `Surrogate-Control: no-store` for Fastly/Cloudflare-like edges
- Remove `ETag`/`Last-Modified` for streaming endpoints so edges won't serve 304s
alex_runtime: also double-check CORS + cookies on the edge. For EventSource with cookies, edge has to forward `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` and mirror the exact `Origin` header. If the edge rewrites to `*` or drops credentials header, Safari will drop the cookie on reconnect which can make the server close the stream.
jordan_acme: customer tried the headers change at origin; when they set `Cache-Control: no-store` on stream responses and turned off ETag they saw stable connections for 30+ mins in Safari. they still reported occasional short reconnects during background tab throttling but nothing like before.
suzanne_support: great. can we capture a recommended config snippet for them to apply and send back as a fix? include server & CDN notes and a tiny SSE server example.
alex_runtime: recommended origin response headers for SSE endpoints:
```
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private
Surrogate-Control: no-store
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.acme.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
```
And make sure the CDN rule for `/stream` paths is: origin-pass-through / cache bypass / no edge caching. remove ETag/Last-Modified on these responses.
alex_runtime: small SSE server example (node/express):
```js
app.get('/stream', (req, res) => {
  res.set({
    'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
    'Cache-Control': 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private',
    'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': 'https://app.acme.com',
    'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials': 'true'
  });
  res.flushHeaders();

  const id = setInterval(() => {
    const payload = JSON.stringify({ts: Date.now(), msg: 'tick'});
    res.write(`data: ${payload}\n\n`);
  }, 1000);

  req.on('close', () => {
    clearInterval(id);
  });
});
```
suzanne_support: also share a short repro curl so they can test origin vs CDN:
```
curl -i -N "https://origin.example.com/stream?room=123" \
  -H "Origin: https://app.acme.com" \
  --cookie "session=eyJ..."
```
`-N` keeps curl streaming.
max_infra: last note on Safari polyfills: polyfills that use XHR can mask the symptom because XHR has different cache semantics and will re-request full ranges. but that's not a true fix. recommend long-term: make SSE endpoints uncached at edge or provide a websocket/long-poll fallback.
jordan_acme: passing this back to customer with the header patch and CDN rule. they asked if we can provide a small diagnostic checklist for our support KB; i can draft it and open a PR. quick checklist idea below:
- Verify the CDN does not cache or revalidate SSE endpoints (no 304s)
- Origin: set Cache-Control: no-store & Surrogate-Control: no-store
- Origin: remove ETag/Last-Modified for SSE path
- Ensure Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true + exact Access-Control-Allow-Origin
- Use cookies with SameSite=None; Secure for cross-site EventSource, or switch to signed query token
- If Safari-only: test bypassing CDN to confirm edge involvement
- Consider websocket or fetch-stream fallback for throttled/background tabs
suzanne_support: perfect — pls open the KB PR and attach these snippets. marking this thread resolved for now; reopen if customer still sees truncation after the CDN rules.
